content.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
content.overview: This lesson covers how to identify and compare the relationships between lines in a coordinate plane by analyzing their slopes. You will learn to distinguish between parallel lines, perpendicular lines, and the special cases of horizontal and vertical lines.
learning_objectives: Calculate the slope of a line using two points or an equation.
Identify parallel lines by comparing their equal slopes.
Identify perpendicular lines by finding negative reciprocal slopes.
Recognize the relationship between horizontal and vertical lines.

sections.title: The Slope-Compare Rule
sections.content:
The slope (m) of a line determines its steepness and direction. To compare two lines, you must first find their slopes. If a line is in slope-intercept form (y = mx + b), the slope is the coefficient 'm'. If you are given two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), use the slope formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1). Once you have the slopes for both lines, you can determine their geometric relationship.

![A flowchart showing how to determine if lines are parallel or perpendicular based on their slopes.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/ac58d779-57ca-471a-bdaf-6f1fe0b95bcf-1786506045015-779.webp)

sections.title: Parallel Lines
sections.content: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if they have the same slope. Parallel lines never intersect because they rise and run at the exact same rate. For example, a line with a slope of 2/3 is parallel to any other line with a slope of 2/3.

sections.title: Perpendicular Lines
sections.content: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if their slopes are negative reciprocals of each other. This means that if you multiply the two slopes together, the product is -1 (m1 * m2 = -1). To find a negative reciprocal, flip the fraction and change the sign. For example, if a line has a slope of 4, the perpendicular slope is -1/4.

sections.title: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
sections.content: Horizontal lines have a slope of 0 and are written in the form y = k. Vertical lines have an undefined slope and are written in the form x = h. Every horizontal line is perpendicular to every vertical line. Note that because vertical lines have undefined slopes, you cannot use the negative reciprocal rule (m1 * m2 = -1) for them; you must recognize them by their equations.

worked_examples.question: Line L passes through the points (1, 2) and (3, 8). What is the slope of a line perpendicular to Line L?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Calculate the slope of Line L using the formula m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1). m = (8 - 2) / (3 - 1) = 6 / 2 = 3. Step 2: Find the negative reciprocal of 3. The reciprocal of 3 (or 3/1) is 1/3. Step 3: Change the sign to make it negative. The perpendicular slope is -1/3.

worked_examples.question:
Which of the following lines is parallel to the line 2x + y = 5?
A. y = 2x + 1
B. y = -2x + 8
C. y = 1/2x - 3
D. x = 2
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Convert the given equation to slope-intercept form (y = mx + b) to find the slope. 2x + y = 5 becomes y = -2x + 5. The slope is -2. Step 2: Identify the choice with the same slope. Choice B (y = -2x + 8) has a slope of -2. Therefore, Choice B is parallel.

common_mistakes: Confusing 'reciprocal' with 'negative reciprocal': Forgetting to change the sign when looking for a perpendicular slope.
Mixing up parallel and perpendicular: Using the same slope for a perpendicular problem or the negative reciprocal for a parallel problem.
Slope calculation errors: Subtracting coordinates in the wrong order (e.g., doing x2 - x1 on top and y2 - y1 on bottom).
Misidentifying slope from standard form: Assuming the slope of Ax + By = C is just A, rather than -A/B.
exam_tips: Always solve for 'y' first to put an equation in y = mx + b form before identifying the slope.
If you see a slope of 0 and an undefined slope, they are perpendicular.
Quick Check: Multiply your two slopes. If the result is -1, they are definitely perpendicular.
Parallel lines must have different y-intercepts; if the slopes and intercepts are both the same, they are the same line, not parallel lines.
content.recap: To master parallel and perpendicular lines, focus on the slope. Parallel lines have equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals (their product is -1). Horizontal lines (slope 0) and vertical lines (undefined slope) are always perpendicular to each other.

knowledge_claims.content: The slope (m) between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is calculated as (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).
Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.
Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes are negative reciprocals, meaning their product is -1.
A horizontal line has a slope of 0 and an equation in the form y = constant.
A vertical line has an undefined slope and an equation in the form x = constant.
Any horizontal line is perpendicular to any vertical line in the coordinate plane.
To find the slope from a linear equation, rewrite it into slope-intercept form (y = mx + b) where m is the slope.
A common error is failing to change the sign when determining the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular slope.
If two lines have the same slope and the same y-intercept, they are the same line (coincident) rather than parallel.
If a line has a slope of 5, a line perpendicular to it must have a slope of -1/5.
To verify if two lines are perpendicular, multiply their slopes; the result must be exactly -1.
Parallel lines in a coordinate plane will never intersect because they maintain a constant distance from each other.

videoLesson.title: Compare Slopes to Identify Perpendicular Lines
videoLesson.description: Recognize and compare slopes from two-point coordinates or y=mx+b. Equal slopes mean parallel; negative reciprocals mean perpendicular; vertical lines are undefined versus horizontal slope 0.
